requirements: STM32F407VGT6 LQFP100 only: PD0=U4:81, AF9 CAN1_RX; reference MB997-E-01 net PD0 reaches P2:34. Physical revision and external attachments remain unconfirmed.
Candidate-specific owned-startup policy, not a vendor mandate: leave P2:34 externally unconnected; enable/read back GPIODEN before GPIO accesses; preserve unrelated gates and fields.
Require PD0 MODER0=0, PUPD0=0, AFSEL0=0 and no active port lock before changing configuration; reject an existing owner. Use aligned32-bit accesses and no lock write sequence.
Set/read back PUPD0=1 (weak pull-up), AFSEL0=9, then MODER0=2 (AF input). Do not drive PD0 as a GPIO output. Leave CAN_TX and all unrelated pins unchanged.

Bound the IDR.ID0 high wait, then check CAN_MSR.RX before requesting initialization exit. A high GPIO sample does not prove 11 consecutive recessive bits or valid CAN timing; INAK/SLAK acknowledgements remain mandatory.
This is a software/model-checked hypothesis candidate. It does not establish electrical timing, fix causality, physical loopback success, transceiver support or external CAN readiness.

requirements: STM32F407VGT6 CAN1 only, owned fresh reset, exclusive CAN1/CAN2 shared filters, PCLK1=42MHz. Registers0x200..0x31C belong only to CAN1, despite shared header structure.
Aligned32-bit accesses. From reset sleep set INRQ and clear SLEEP; bound INAK/SLAK acknowledgements. Program BTR only while INAK=1. Preserve DBF and use NART/RFLM=1.
Combined SILM/LBKM=1 provides internal loopback with CANRX disconnected and CANTX recessive; external CAN wiring/transceiver is not established.
BRP5,TS1=10,TS2=1,SJW0 gives42MHz/(6*(1+11+2))=500kbit/s nominal; sample point12/14. This is calculated, not physically measured.

FINIT=1 during filter configuration, bank0 inactive before writes, single32-bit identifier list, FIFO0, FR1=FR2=0x123<<21, only bank0 active. Retain CAN2SB14 and preserve FMR reserved bits read from hardware. Full reset word remains unasserted due to source table presentation differences.

Mailbox reset data and filter values are unspecified. Require empty TX mailboxes and FIFOs with no stale completion/error; explicitly write all four TX mailbox0 registers, TXRQ last. Never write pending TX or any RX mailbox.

One standard data frame,ID0x123,DLC8, no extended/remote/time-trigger traffic. Require request-complete,TXOK0,TME0 and full matching received identifier,length,payload. Errors have precedence over simultaneous progress.

Read all four FIFO words before literal RFOM0; never RMW mixed W1C/release status. Bound release acknowledgement. Preserve underrun/overrun/bus-off/transmit diagnostics on failure; require owned reset before retry.
Interrupt delivery uses the separate FIFO0 IRQ contract; polling completion alone cannot prove exception delivery. No normal external-bus,CAN2,FD,DMA or broad recovery support.
This revised candidate requires the explicit GPIO can1_rx_pd0 route before CAN configuration; no claim is made that every silent-loopback implementation requires this pin choice.

Require CAN_MSR.RX high while INAK=1 before clearing INRQ. A low snapshot rejects the attempt without enabling IRQ or TX. After clearing INRQ retain a finite wait for INAK/SLAK=0; hardware synchronization still needs 11 consecutive recessive bits.

RM0090 describes actual CANRX disregard in established combined silent/loopback operation; do not use that wording to erase initialization synchronization prerequisites. The prior physical failure is preserved and the proposed fix is not yet physically tested.
silent_loopback.title: CAN1 silent internal loopback, standard0x123 eight-byte one-shot

requirements: Keep global interrupts masked during handler/state/configuration and arming. IRQ20/vector36 must resolve CAN1_RX0_IRQHandler in the pinned startup asset.
Clear source cause before NVIC pending, program implemented priority5, enable only FMPIE0, then NVIC line20. Restore intended global interrupt state last, after staging the owned request.
Handler validates error/state and all four receive words, releases FIFO with literal RFOM0, then disables source and owned line. Spurious interrupts cannot establish success.

A bounded foreground wait requires both valid interrupt-delivered receive and TX completion; polling/FMP or TXOK alone cannot pass. Failure cleanup disables only owned source/line without erasing diagnostics. Reset before retry.
This revised candidate requires the explicit GPIO can1_rx_pd0 route before CAN configuration; no claim is made that every silent-loopback implementation requires this pin choice.

Require CAN_MSR.RX high while INAK=1 before clearing INRQ. A low snapshot rejects the attempt without enabling IRQ or TX. After clearing INRQ retain a finite wait for INAK/SLAK=0; hardware synchronization still needs 11 consecutive recessive bits.

RM0090 describes actual CANRX disregard in established combined silent/loopback operation; do not use that wording to erase initialization synchronization prerequisites. The prior physical failure is preserved and the proposed fix is not yet physically tested.
